public_health_question.v: What was the likely source of Legionnaires disease in a U.S. traveler who stayed in a private vacation rental in USVI, and what environmental conditions favored Legionella growth?

ev.q: VIDOH requested assistance from CDC’s Legionella program to conduct environmental sampling and testing for Legionella bacteria.
Legionnaires Disease in a U.S. Traveler After Staying in a Private Vacation Rental House in the U.S. Virgin Islands
was notified of a confirmed case of Legionnaires disease in an adult U.S. resident
Interviews with the patient indicated that he had stayed at a privately owned vacation rental property during January 15–22.
Twenty-five bulk water, swab, and cartridge filter samples were collected at the property.
he had stayed at a privately owned vacation rental property during January 15–22.

equity.level_reason: Single case report; the patient's age and sex are descriptors only. Resource constraints refer to the territory (geography), not a social-position dimension.

level_alternative.reason: Resource-constrained setting of USVI could be read as an SES-like descriptor, though geography alone is not an SPD.

equity.equity_measurement: Resource-constrained territory setting (USVI) is geography, not an SPD.

notes: Single-case report with environmental sampling; the only quantity is the share of 25 environmental samples positive (11, 44%). The urinary antigen test only confirms case status and is not a procedure. The patient also tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, recorded only as a coinfection.
view_issues: Text says 11 positive locations and 44% of samples; 11/25 = 44%, consistent if each location is one sample.
